title: Starting violin at eight and a trip west
summary: A full-size violin put him off at first. His mother took him to California and then Chicago for her health, and the early Creole band in California is mentioned.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Just to kind of get into your New Orleans sources, had you started on violin while you were in school, in grammar school?

Yes. I started violin when I was about eight years old, but the violin teacher made a mistake. He bought me a full-size violin, and I struggled along for a few months and got disgusted. I didn't know. I was only eight years old. I didn't know if it was the reason. It wasn't until years later that the next violin teacher I got told me, said, that guy is crazy. He shouldn't have started doing a full-size violin. You can't reach your hand. I was having an awful difficulty trying to play the thing, see? And so I didn't bother with it until I think I was about 12 years old, from about eight to 12, about four years. Meanwhile, my mother, we went to California. She took a trip for her health. New Orleans was full of mosquitoes in those days. Took a trip for her health. We went to Oakland, stayed there about six months, went to San Francisco, and then we went to Chicago, came here to Chicago. And then we went back to New Orleans.
San Francisco, do you remember any of the jazz men being?
No, I don't remember any of those. I was too little then.
The first migration, an early migration, I should say, an early migration, and the Creole band, which included Kepler, was out there. They were out there, uh-huh. In maybe 11, 1911.
